patch_description:
The current search uses 8 restarts of 30,000 iterations, a single log-sum-exp tail scale schedule, 90% active-triple point selection, and one-point random perturbations. Its main limitation is that early log-sum-exp pressure can concentrate on a small set of currently active determinants before a globally favorable combinatorial structure is discovered.

This revision uses 11 shorter but more diverse restarts, including boundary-biased simplex initializations, and a phase-dependent lower-tail objective. Early search rewards the mean of the lowest 30 determinants and a broad soft-min surrogate, encouraging global separation. The tail width is progressively narrowed to 10 determinants while the exact minimum receives increasing weight during the final phase. Proposals use barycentric-weight perturbations rather than Cartesian clipping, preserving simplex feasibility more smoothly. A small proportion of coordinated two-point moves helps escape poor oriented-matroid cells. Final polishing uses active-set directions plus random tangential simplex directions and prioritizes exact maximin improvement.
